evidence.exact_quote: All file paths computed relative to a worktree root MUST be normalized via `realpath()` before any scope check or file guard comparison.

items.impact: A new file or directory does not yet have a resolvable realpath, so a literal implementation either denies legitimate creation or invents an unchecked parent-resolution exception.
items.statement: The fail-closed path rule does not define how creation targets that do not yet exist are validated; it needs an explicit canonical-parent plus single-component containment contract and falsifying traversal/symlink tests.
items.title: Realpath rule is incomplete for creation targets

evidence.exact_quote: Before building `IterationContext`, optionally verify the worktree path still exists and is still in `git worktree list`; if not, remove from `active_worktrees` and fall back to main repo (and log).

items.impact: A stale worktree binding can redirect an attempt into the shared main repository, violating isolation and potentially mutating the wrong workspace.
items.statement: Falling back to the main repo after worktree validation failure contradicts the later exact-targeting rule that rejects restore or retry rather than substituting another worktree; invalid bindings must block, not silently change execution context.
items.title: Invalid worktree fallback breaks isolation

evidence.exact_quote: **Until config wiring is fixed**, worktrees and Git behavior cannot be fully controlled from the UI.

items.impact: GUI settings can appear effective while the orchestrator runs defaults, making worktree and Git behavior operationally misleading.
items.statement: The document explicitly identifies config projection as a release-order blocker and requires Phase 1 before worktree or Git behavior can be trusted from the UI.
items.title: Run-start config projection is a critical prerequisite

evidence.exact_quote: If building run config from `gui_config` fails (e.g. missing required field), fall back to `ConfigManager::discover_with_hint(hint)`; if that also fails, fail the run with a clear error (do not start with default-only config silently).

items.impact: A malformed current setting can cause the run to use older disk configuration while the UI still claims that current settings govern the run.
items.statement: The fallback contract does not say how the UI discloses that current in-memory settings were rejected, nor which fields may safely come from disk; this conflicts with the statement that Run always uses current UI state.
items.title: Config fallback can silently replace current UI state

evidence.exact_quote: Verify with a run: toggle "Enable parallel execution", save, start run → worktrees are created when applicable.
With "Enable parallel execution" on and no Save, start run → worktrees are created when applicable.

items.impact: Following the checklist can pass while the defining no-Save behavior remains broken.
items.statement: The Phase 1 checklist requires Save before verification, but the phase acceptance oracle explicitly requires no Save; the checklist must test the harder no-Save case.
items.title: Phase 1 checklist masks the no-Save requirement

evidence.exact_quote: Config Format Mismatch Resolution (Resolved — Migrate to Single Canonical Format):

items.impact: Implementers can reasonably choose incompatible Option A migration or Option B projection architectures and produce different persistence and failure behavior.
items.statement: The document selects Option B as canonical, then labels migration to one canonical format as resolved, while its risks discuss Option A conditionally; the release contract does not clearly retire one strategy.
items.title: Option A and Option B are both presented as resolved

evidence.exact_quote: **Conflict persistence:** In-memory only for initial release -- `HashSet<node_id>` of conflict worktrees; optional Phase 6: `.puppet-master/worktree-conflicts.json`.

items.impact: After restart, rerunning the same node can remove the preserved conflict worktree and destroy unresolved user state.
items.statement: The initial-release decision knowingly makes conflict protection session-only even though restart is the adversarial boundary that originally causes overwrite; durable conflict lineage is required before rerun is allowed.
items.title: Conflict preservation is lost on restart

evidence.exact_quote: when the compare target is gone, pruned, or otherwise a `stale-target`, open the nearest valid baseline when one exists, explain the stale-target downgrade, and offer alternate pivots.

items.impact: A review may display a technically valid but semantically different diff, leading users to approve or diagnose against the wrong baseline.
items.statement: Automatically opening the nearest baseline after target loss is unsafe unless the replacement is visually non-dismissible and no review/approval action can proceed until the user confirms the new identity.
items.title: Stale review targets are automatically substituted

evidence.exact_quote: W-003 remains addressable as a fine-grained Worktree/Git PlanUnit with source-span coverage.

items.impact: Migration and indexing validators can pass without proving the config blocker, GUI copy selection, or owner behavior described by these units.
items.statement: W-002 and W-003 acceptance criteria verify addressability and lineage preservation, not the product/runtime assertions in canonical_text; executable or behavior-specific oracles are absent.
items.title: PlanUnit acceptance does not test canonical behavior

evidence.exact_quote: Worktree-relative paths must be realpath-normalized, fail closed on resolution failure, validated against canonical roots, and use no-follow traversal by default unless an explicit Follow symlinks setting revalidates the resolved target.

items.impact: This materially constrains traversal and symlink escape implementations and preserves fail-closed scope enforcement.
items.statement: W-004 explicitly binds canonical-root validation, fail-closed resolution, and no-follow defaults rather than leaving path containment to builder discretion.
items.title: Path guard policy is explicitly fail closed

evidence.exact_quote: Chat worktree create/remove delegates to WorktreeManager; worktree creation/removal is user or system infrastructure rather than agent-tool-gated raw bash, and git-aware tools auto-scope to the worktree through process cwd.

items.impact: Centralizing lifecycle commands prevents agents from bypassing identity, safety, and cleanup policy with raw subprocesses.
items.statement: W-005 clearly assigns worktree creation/removal authority to WorktreeManager and forbids raw agent-managed add/remove commands.
items.title: Worktree lifecycle authority is centralized

evidence.exact_quote: Assistant/worktree row compare actions open committed branch-to-branch review through cmd.git.open_diff with compare_origin set to the base branch ref, and orch-owned worktree rows show Open Lane rather than Open Thread.

items.impact: Users may believe Compare includes dirty or staged changes when it only compares branch HEADs.
items.statement: The command semantics are precise, but the unit does not require a committed-only label, dirty-change warning, or oracle that prevents the GUI from implying a complete worktree diff.
items.title: Compare action can misrepresent uncommitted state

evidence.exact_quote: Worktree creation uses the configured base branch or explicit ref and handles existing branches by verifying refs and reusing safe existing branches without unsafe deletion.
Detached worktrees and missing merge target branches must be detected and handled with clear skip, create, or error behavior rather than empty-branch merges or blind checkout failure.

items.impact: Different builders can checkout versus use a ref, or skip versus create versus error on the same repository state, yielding incompatible and potentially destructive behavior.
items.statement: W-007 and W-012 preserve alternatives instead of a closed transition table: precedence for configured base versus explicit ref, the definition of safe reuse, and the missing-target outcome remain undecided.
items.title: Branch creation and merge outcomes remain open choices

evidence.exact_quote: After restart, worktree resolution and PR head branch resolution recover from durable or listed worktrees instead of falling back to the main repo path or main repo branch.
Merge-conflict worktrees must not be silently removed or overwritten on rerun; reuse remains blocked until resolution or explicit discard preserves user-visible conflict state.

items.impact: A listed worktree keyed only by node can be rebound to the wrong run or attempt, and conflict protection cannot be enforced after session memory is lost.
items.statement: The units require restart recovery and conflict preservation but do not bind recovery to lane/run/attempt lineage or require durable conflict state, leaving collision and stale-reuse behavior underspecified.
items.title: Restart recovery lacks durable lineage disambiguation

evidence.exact_quote: Conflict state may surface the worktree path or status and a Resolve worktree conflicts action for user repair or confirmed removal.

items.impact: An implementation can satisfy the unit while exposing no actionable recovery path for a blocked conflict.
items.statement: The word may leaves the only user repair/removal affordance optional even though conflict preservation intentionally blocks reuse.
items.title: Conflict recovery UI is not required

evidence.exact_quote: Node IDs used as path components and branch IDs used as Git refs must be sanitized with shared/ref-safe helpers before join or branch creation.

items.impact: The shared helper requirement reduces traversal, invalid-ref, and inconsistent-normalization risk.
items.statement: W-011 explicitly treats node and branch identifiers as untrusted structural inputs and requires shared sanitization before use.
items.title: Node and branch identifiers are explicitly sanitized

evidence.exact_quote: Lanes own worktrees through explicit Source Control allocation, Orchestrator records the handshake, and canonical lane/worktree records drive reuse, cleanup, retry, and recovery.

items.impact: A crash after filesystem allocation but before ledger recording can create an unowned worktree; the inverse ordering can create a record pointing to no worktree.
items.statement: W-013 names both handshake sides but defines no idempotency key, commit ordering, compensation, recovery scan, or observable intermediate state for partial allocation failures.
items.title: Allocation handshake lacks crash-consistent semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Worktree rows show owning package, lane, run, lifecycle, and blocked/recovery state while Source Control actions report results back through canonical lane/worktree records.
Orchestrator and Progress surfaces consume a first-class SCM status strip with primary and additional active contexts, lifecycle states, blocked episode CTAs, and exact deep-link payload fields.

items.impact: Large numbers of contexts or long localized identifiers can overflow or become inaccessible, and stale state can look live without explicit projection-age semantics.
items.statement: The row and status-strip contracts enumerate data but provide no scale limit, virtualization/overflow behavior, screen-reader ordering, keyboard flow, localization constraints, or stale-data acceptance oracle.
items.title: Ownership status UI lacks scale and accessibility contracts

evidence.exact_quote: Worktree allocation follows lane/effective-scope provider policy; contamination, dirty state, conflict state, blocked recovery, or lineage mismatch disqualifies reuse, and cleanup waits for grace-period and file-lock checks.

items.impact: A new owner, safe-point reference, or editor lock can appear after checks and before deletion, allowing deletion of a newly active worktree.
items.statement: Grace-period and file-lock checks are not an atomic deletion fence; cleanup needs a compare-and-delete generation, ownership lease, or equivalent transaction and a race oracle.
items.title: Cleanup checks permit a TOCTOU deletion race

evidence.exact_quote: Worktree transfer, restore, retry, and fresh-attempt payloads carry explicit SCM targeting and never silently inherit prior ownership; legacy git_panel/* state is one-time migration input only.
Source Control owns live SCM truth with stable project_id/repo_id/worktree_id; remote or SSH and historical worktrees keep correct live, historical, or compare contexts with deterministic labels.

items.impact: Explicit durable IDs and one-way migration materially reduce stale ownership inheritance and remote/local identity confusion.
items.statement: W-016 and W-017 establish explicit SCM targeting, stable canonical identities, and a no-dual-write legacy migration boundary.
items.title: Runtime and remote SCM identity is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: User-facing action nouns, receipt nouns, worktree glossary terms, blocked reason-family templates, and SCM receipt lineage remain distinct and typed across Source Control, Orchestrator, GitHub Actions, Docker, Kubernetes, and history views.

items.impact: Translations can collapse distinct actions or artifacts, breaking the semantic distinctions the unit requires and confusing assistive labels.
items.statement: The typed-English vocabulary is strong, but no locale-stable message IDs, translator context, forbidden synonym tests, or accessible-name mapping preserves those distinctions across localization.
items.title: Typed copy lacks a localization preservation contract

evidence.exact_quote: Worktree state files are documented, Doctor adds worktree checks and orphan detection, and optional path/list revalidation can remove stale active_worktrees before use.

items.impact: Initial-release execution can trust stale in-memory paths and operate in a removed, moved, or repurposed directory.
items.statement: Path/list revalidation protects the execution boundary and should be mandatory before use; making it optional is inconsistent with fail-closed worktree targeting.
items.title: Worktree path revalidation is optional

evidence.exact_quote: Git exit scenarios map to success, informational, retryable, or fatal outcomes, with bounded retry only for network timeout and lock contention cases allowed by the table.
Mutating or validation-sensitive git commands treat non-zero as hard error except nothing to commit, and verify staged state after git add before accepting commit-sensitive transitions.

items.impact: Localized stderr/stdout, partial clone state, concurrent index mutation, or ambiguous retry counting can misclassify failures or accept a staged state that changed after verification.
items.statement: The policy needs locale-independent nothing-to-commit detection, explicit retry-versus-attempt counting and partial-operation cleanup, plus a repository/index lock or generation check around post-add verification and commit.
items.title: Git recovery classification is brittle under text and races

evidence.exact_quote: GitManager and Doctor resolve git through the same helper instead of allowing PATH-only runtime behavior to diverge from Doctor fallback resolution.

items.impact: Doctor and runtime cannot disagree merely because they searched for the Git binary through different algorithms.
items.statement: W-023 provides a clear single-source resolution contract shared by diagnostic and runtime consumers.
items.title: Git binary resolution has one owner

evidence.exact_quote: PR creation uses the GitHub HTTPS API and Doctor validates API auth state and required scopes; runtime PR creation must not shell out to a GitHub CLI.

items.impact: Expired credentials, rate limits, timeouts after server-side creation, or duplicate retries can leave the user with an unknown or duplicate PR state.
items.statement: The API-only authority boundary is explicit, but runtime auth refresh, offline/rate-limit handling, idempotent lookup after ambiguous timeout, secret-safe logging, and failure-state GUI oracles are absent.
items.title: PR API contract omits ambiguous-failure recovery

evidence.exact_quote: Git configured and repo checks consider project-local context, passing when usable global or local identity exists and running repo checks in the active project path when known.

items.impact: A Doctor fix can inspect or initialize an unrelated CWD/HOME repository when the active project context is absent or stale.
items.statement: The phrase when known leaves the no-project authority boundary open; mutating fixes should require explicit project identity and fail closed rather than fall back to ambient directories.
items.title: Doctor fallback can act on the wrong repository

segments.summary: Reviewed path containment, worktree lifecycle and recovery, lineage identity, Git subprocess policy, and Source Control topology under exact and adversarial lenses; found unsafe fallback and a creation-path contract gap alongside the explicit config blocker.

Reviewed review/conflict UX, run-start projection, implementation order, acceptance tables, resolved decisions, DRY boundaries, and lifecycle addenda; found stale substitutions, competing config strategies, contradictory tests, and restart-unsafe conflict persistence.
Reviewed historical safe-point/lane reconciliation and W-002 through W-005, confirming explicit path and authority constraints while identifying metadata-only PlanUnit acceptance criteria.

Reviewed W-006 through W-012 for compare truth, branch transitions, restart recovery, conflict handling, and identifier safety; found misleading compare scope, open transition choices, non-durable recovery, and optional repair UI.

Reviewed W-013 through W-018 for handshake, row projection, allocation, cleanup, migration, identity, remote context, and multi-context UI; found crash-consistency, TOCTOU, scale, and accessibility gaps while confirming exact identity boundaries.

Reviewed W-019 through W-025 for typed copy, diagnostics, Git exit and staging integrity, binary resolution, GitHub API authority, and project context; found localization, stale-context, concurrency, ambiguous API failure, and ambient-repository authority gaps.

Does the runtime contract require allocation handshakes and cleanup deletion to use durable idempotency keys or storage transactions?
Which config strategy is canonical for initial release: Option B run-start projection only, or migration to a single canonical persisted format?

Git locale-independent detection of nothing-to-commit and ambiguous push or PR retries
Accessible scalable multi-worktree status and commit graph interaction patterns
